Anna — thanks for the questionnaire and the three callouts. Answers below are intentionally concise; happy to expand in the follow-up call or with specific workbook rows.

1) Admin vs end-user telemetry
- We separate telemetry streams: admin console telemetry (actions by named admin users, audit logs) and product usage telemetry (anonymous usage metrics).
- Admin logs: include admin user-id, timestamp, action, resource id. We persist admin logs for 3 years by default; retention is configurable per customer.
- Product usage: aggregated events, no PII by default. IPs are captured in transient logs for throttling and abuse detection and are purged from long-term analytics.

2) Cookies (docs site vs admin console)
- Docs site: uses a single necessary cookie for session/CSRF plus an opt-in analytics cookie (first-party) for page performance; no third-party advertising cookies.
- Admin console: uses same session cookie + secure, HttpOnly authentication cookie. Optional feature flag cookies may be set for UX.
- We do use a third-party analytics provider for aggregated docs traffic (opt-in) — we can provide the provider name and subprocessors.

3) SOC 2 status
- Current status: In scope for SOC 2 Type II; the control audit window is Q2 2027, report expected Q3 2027.
- Short term: we provide compensating controls and can accept contract language for a remediation roadmap if your procurement requires a report earlier.

HIPAA contact
- For HIPAA/HIPAA-specific scoping please use security@redwood.com. I'll loop our compliance lead in the calendar invite for the follow-up.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Timeline.pdf (brief timeline + key milestones).
